_comment: Every scheduled run writes one record here — including, especially, a run that could not connect. A failed run that logs is data; a failed run that stays silent is a hole in the record, and a hole is indistinguishable from a run that never fired. Record shape: { date, slot: open|hourly|preclose|retro, at, fired, connected, actions, note }. 'connected' means the brokerage connector attached and the run read live account state; a run that reasoned only from this repo's JSON is fired=true, connected=false. Per-run rows begin on recordsBeginOn. Anything earlier is carried in priorSummary as an aggregate, because those runs predate this file and the per-run detail was never written down. Do not backfill it.

scheduler.note: True as of 2026-08-05: a scheduled run has now fired and recorded its own row. Read it narrowly. This is a desktop scheduled task, not a server-side runner — it fires only while the operator's Claude app is open, so a missed window runs late on next launch rather than on time, and the first row here is itself an example: the retro slot is 16:30 ET and it fired at 00:45 ET. Every run therefore checks how late it fired and refuses to write an order specification if the quotes it would rest on are stale. 'Configured' means a trigger exists and has fired, not that the four slots fire reliably at their stated times.

slots.name: Market open
slots.does: Verify the connector attached before reasoning about anything. Check settled cash, apply exit rules, run the six-item pre-trade checklist.

slots.name: Mid-session
slots.does: Enforce exits the hour a level is hit. Default is no trade.

slots.name: Pre-close
slots.does: Exit discipline. Decide overnight holds explicitly rather than by default. Close option no-fly windows.

slots.name: Retro
slots.does: Read-only. Grades the day against the rules outcome-blind, then runs the standing rule-drift check. Never places an order.

priorSummary.note: Zero, deliberately. Five firings were recorded here on 2026-08-04, but the operator has confirmed they were setup tests rather than live scheduled runs, so they are excluded from run health — counting a test as a run would overstate how much of this system has actually operated. They are set to zero rather than deleted, and this note stays, because the correction is part of the record. Run health now reads from live runs only, of which there are none yet.

runs.note: Stopped at the scope preflight: the private mandate's targetAccountId is unset, so there is no account this run is permitted to read. Nothing was reconciled and nothing was graded. Also fired at 00:45 ET rather than its 16:30 slot — a desktop trigger running the window late, recorded as it happened.

Stopped on the staleness guard: fired at 00:53 ET, roughly nine hours and twenty minutes past the 15:33 ET pre-close window it was scheduled for, so the hold-or-exit decision this slot exists to make was never made inside the window. No order specification was written and the connector was not attached — a pre-close proposal resting on quotes nine hours dead is not a proposal, and publishing one would put a stale instruction on the board. The mandate was readable and its targetAccountId is set this time, so scope was not the blocker; lateness was.

Stopped on the staleness guard: fired at 00:57 ET, outside the 10:00-15:00 ET window entirely — 9h40m past the last 8/4 hourly slot and hours before the first 8/5 one, with the market closed in between. No quotes were read, the connector was not attached, and no order specification was written. This run's job is exits, so the honest statement of what was lost is that if a stop or target was hit during 8/4's session, this slot did not enforce it; the open positions list in state.json is empty as last written, but that file is not live state and this run did not verify it. The mandate was readable and its targetAccountId is set, so scope was not the blocker; lateness was.

Stopped on the staleness guard, but from the other side: fired at 00:53 ET, eight hours and forty minutes BEFORE the 09:33 window rather than after it, with the market shut and no session yet to analyse. The connector did attach and the scope preflight passed on an exact identifier match, so live state was read and refreshed - settled cash 28.96, unsettled 99.94 settling this morning, no open equity or option positions and therefore no exit due. No order specification was written: there are no live quotes eight hours before an open, and the day-2 continuation trigger this slot was watching cannot be evaluated before the day exists.

Second retro row today and the first one able to do the job: the 00:45 row above stopped at the scope preflight because the mandate was unset, the operator set it at 00:47 ET, and this run re-fired and matched the identifier exactly. Still 8h28m past the 16:30 ET 8/4 slot, which costs a retro nothing - it grades a session that has already settled and writes no specification. Reconciled both AMD legs against the API, appended 8/4's official settled closes to bench, graded the one ungraded entry, and ran the drift check. Zero actions, as always: this slot has no order authority.

The first run in this record to fire inside its own window: 09:40 ET against a 09:33 slot, seven minutes late, so the staleness guard passed and the session was live to read. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. Settled cash is 128.90 with nothing unsettled - the 99.94 the 00:53 row saw pending has cleared, so the two figures the board carried separately are now one number, and deployable is the whole balance. No equity or option positions are open, so no exit was due. No specification written: the branch the tape resolved to is the stand-aside one. AMD's 8/4 print gapped it down to a 491.73 bid against a 518.58 close, which kills the day-2 continuation setup this slot was watching and, with the leader red, kills the sympathy-laggard read that depended on it. UPST is the only name with a live catalyst and it is trading its reaction day at a 32.23 bid, +6.3% - checklist item 2 forbids exactly that entry, so the checklist stopped there in order.

First hourly to fire inside its own window: 10:22 ET against the 10:17 slot, five minutes late, so the staleness guard passed and the quotes were live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. Re-read live: no equity positions, no option positions, cash 128.90 with nothing unsettled - so there was no target, stop, time stop or option no-fly window to enforce, which is the only job this slot has. No specification written. The entry question was not reopened on its own merits: the bar for a new mid-session entry is higher than at the open, and the one name with a live catalyst is UPST, still trading its reaction day at a 32.36 bid, +6.7%, which is the entry checklist item 2 names a wait signal. AMD extended its gap down to a 486.55 bid, -6.2%, so the setup this board was watching is further from valid than it was at 09:42, not closer. Standing aside with the position unchanged.

_rowFields: trigger: 'scheduled' when the scheduler fired this run in its own window, 'manual' when a human invoked it. Only scheduled rows count toward run health - a manual invocation proves the code path works, not that the system runs. declined: true when the run deliberately stopped on a guard (fired outside its window, or the mandate was unset) and therefore never attempted to reach the broker. A decline is correct behaviour, not a connection failure, and it is excluded from the run-health denominator rather than counted against it.
